source: Zhao et al. (2024) CogLM: Piaget-based cognitive ability benchmark for language models
finding: Benchmark built on Piaget's theory, 1,220 questions over 10 abilities, written by 20+ experts. GPT-4 reaches about a 20-year-old human level.
numbers: 1,220 questions; 10 abilities in 4 stages; abstract says GPT-4 comparable to a 20-year-old.
limits: Abstract page only for this line; details in c02-c04.
agent_relevance: Gives a stage-ordered test we could reuse to check an agent's reasoning level.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) CogLM: Piaget-based cognitive ability benchmark for language models
finding: Overall calibrated accuracy rises with model size and maps to a human age equivalent. Humans: 141 valid respondents aged 6-20.
numbers: OPT 125M 7.1% (age 4.8); OPT 6.7B 15.5% (6.5); Llama-2 7B 20.5% (7.3); Llama-2 70B 54.6% (14.1); GPT-3.5-Turbo 64.0% (16.1); GPT-4 84.7% (20.0); adult human 93.7% (21.5). Age vs score Spearman 0.717. Held-out age prediction Spearman 0.935.
limits: Age mapping is a regression fit, stage weights only as ratios 1:2.6:1.4:2.5. Table lists identical 54.6 for Llama-2 70B base and chat (possible copy error). Calibrated for guessing.
agent_relevance: Age-equivalent framing is shaky but shows scale, not stage order, drives scores.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) CogLM: Piaget-based cognitive ability benchmark for language models
finding: Per-ability profile: GPT-4 near human on early stages, weakest on planning and propositional operations (formal stage). Conservation 90.4 vs human 98.2.
numbers: GPT-4: constancy 96.0 (human 100); conservation 90.4 (98.2); reversibility 78.7 (92.0); induction 78.7 (91.6); hypothetico-deductive 99.4 (100); propositional 61.0 (82.0); planning 59.4 (95.6). GPT-3.5 planning 6.7. GPT-4 empathy 90.3 vs human 84.2.
limits: Tasks are text scenarios, not child-style hands-on tasks. Small per-ability item counts.
agent_relevance: Planning is the large LLM gap vs humans, matching the agent need for an explicit plan state.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) CogLM: Piaget-based cognitive ability benchmark for language models
finding: Prompt tricks barely help; adding cognitive reasoning written by a stronger model helps a small model.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo: base 64.0, CoT 64.3, self-consistency T0.3 64.4, T0.7 63.1. Chain-of-Cognition on Llama-2-chat-7B: 31.0 -> 38.1.
limits: Only GPT-3.5 for CoT, one small model for Chain-of-Cognition.
agent_relevance: Structure from a stronger teacher helps weak models; CoT alone adds about 0.3 points.

source: Luo et al. (2024) Vision Language Models Know Law of Conservation without Understanding More-or-Less (ConserveBench)
finding: VLMs pass transformation (reversibility) conservation tasks but fail non-transformation quantity tasks, a dissociation not seen in children.
numbers: 365 experiments (volume, solid quantity, length, number; 95 number tasks). GPT-4o 97.44% transformational; 31.22% non-transformational single-image; 22.11% number tasks. Overall at most 38%.
limits: 5 VLMs, zero-shot only, no CoT comparison, no human baseline. 'Dense equals more' is a hypothesis. Model list inconsistent in text.
agent_relevance: A model can show the Piagetian signature on one probe yet lack the concept; test several probes per concept.

source: ConservationBench: conservation and control bias in VLMs, arXiv 2603.07109 (2026)
finding: 112 VLMs, 384 videos (192 conserving, 192 non-conserving controls). High conservation accuracy is a default-invariance bias, reversing on controls.
numbers: Human 98.35% vs model averages 20-69% (chance 33.3%). gemini-2.5-pro 69.11 avg (conserve 94.33, control 43.88); gpt-5 63.65 (91.48/35.82); claude-sonnet-4-5 60.41 (75.43/45.39). Conserve vs control r=-0.510. 82/112 models (73.2%) below 10% on strict pairwise scoring.
limits: Perceptual judgement only; behavioural; abstract says 'near chance' but top models reach 60-69% average.
agent_relevance: Matched control items are needed: a right answer on the classic item may be a heuristic.

source: ConservationBench: conservation and control bias in VLMs, arXiv 2603.07109 (2026)
finding: Blank images give 85.7% 'conserve' answers: the text prior drives the answer. Chain-of-thought hurt on number and length. Size does not predict accuracy.
numbers: Blank-image conserve rate 85.7%; text-only 73.7%; real visuals about 60%. CoT worse on Number&Length F(3,333)=18.28, p<0.001. Frame count no effect (p=0.416). Params 1B-76B vs conservation R2=0.019.
limits: Prompt effects only on some properties; Volume&Size had no prompt effect (p=0.114).
agent_relevance: CoT is not a free scaffold; it can lower accuracy where perception matters.

source: Li et al. (2024-25) Core Knowledge Deficits in Multi-Modal Language Models (CoreCognition)
finding: CoreCognition: 1,503 questions over 12 core abilities mapped to Piaget stages, 230 models. Models lag humans most on low-level (sensorimotor, concrete) abilities.
numbers: Human mean 86.98%. GPT-o1 74.91, GPT-4o 69.25, Qwen2.5-VL-72B 68.29. Gaps to humans on lower stages 15.91, 21.57, 22.53 points. Perspective taking worst and declines with scale.
limits: Stage labels (4 sensorimotor, 5 concrete, 3 formal) are the authors' mapping. Paper text has small count inconsistencies (11 vs 10 prompts).
agent_relevance: Model scale helps high-level more than low-level skills: grounded basics are not fixed by scale.

source: Li et al. (2024-25) Core Knowledge Deficits in Multi-Modal Language Models (CoreCognition)
finding: Reasoning models do not beat instruction-tuned ones on most abilities; most prompts fail; concept-hacking shows shortcuts.
numbers: Reasoning vs instruct no significant difference on 10 of 12 abilities; Perspective Taking worse for reasoning models (P=0.0037). A cognitive instruction prompt gave over +6%. 45 concept-hacking pairs with inverted answers: almost no model balanced.
limits: Concept hacking set is small (45).
agent_relevance: Inverted-answer control pairs are a cheap check we can copy for scaffold audits.

source: Li et al. (2024) CogDevelop2K: Reversed Cognitive Development in Multimodal LLMs
finding: Models show a reversed trajectory: better at formal operations than at concrete operations.
numbers: 2,519 questions (1,677 single-frame, 842 multi-frame). GPT-family accuracy approx sensorimotor 0.4-0.6, concrete 0.2-0.4, formal 0.6-0.8. Concept-explanation prompt: GPT-4o High 0.555 -> 0.636 (+0.081), GPT-4V Turbo 0.519 -> 0.586, GPT-4o Mini 0.487 -> 0.547.
limits: Per-stage numbers only as ranges. Model count inconsistent (46 vs 48). Stage mapping is authors' own.
agent_relevance: Stage order does not hold for LLMs, so do not design the agent as a developmental ladder.

source: Milicka et al. (2024) Large language models are able to downplay their cognitive abilities to fit the persona they simulate (PLOS One)
finding: GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4 playing children aged 1-6 on false-belief tasks. GPT-4 tracks the real developmental curve better but is hyper-accurate in some prompts.
numbers: 1,296 trials; temps 0, 0.5, 0.9; kappa 0.88 on 30% double-coding. Real children: 3-year-olds often fail location task, most correct from age 4 to 4.5.
limits: English only; per-age numbers only in figures; GPT-4 base model unavailable so the RLHF explanation is a guess.
agent_relevance: Prompting a model to act at a lower stage partly works, so a reasoning-level knob may be controllable.

source: Milicka et al. (2024) Large language models are able to downplay their cognitive abilities to fit the persona they simulate (PLOS One)
finding: Prompt type matters: primed-by-corpus (CHILDES excerpts) matched ages best; CoT helped GPT-4 but GPT-3.5 simulated experts. Language complexity rose with age, steepest between years 1 and 2.
numbers: About 100 CHILDES replicas per excerpt, ten excerpts per age group. Temperature, child gender, parent gender: no consistent effect. Unexpected-content task harder than change-of-location.
limits: Primed-by-corpus gave lowest linguistic complexity, so surface style and reasoning separate.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples of the target level beat instructions alone.

source: Kosinski and Sap false-belief LLM results as cited in Milicka 2024 (secondhand)
finding: Earlier text false-belief tests showed fast climb across model generations.
numbers: Kosinski: davinci-001/002 10%, davinci-003 and GPT-3.5-turbo 35%, GPT-4 90%. Sap: GPT-3 up to 60% vs 90-100% for humans.
limits: Secondhand via the review in c11; original papers not opened.
agent_relevance: Contamination and wording sensitivity make these unreliable as stage tests.

source: ChildAgentEval: cognitive age alignment in interactive agents, arXiv 2605.17894 (2026)
finding: Telling a model its age gives flat or wrong trajectories; skill-guided prompting gives monotone age scaling. Based on WISC-IV factors, not Piaget tasks.
numbers: GPT-5.4 age-label prompt: 0.53 at 7, 0.46 at 13, 0.52 at 16; Spearman age vs score -0.40. Skill-guided: 0.41 (ages 6-8) to 0.50 (15-17), Spearman 1.00; others 0.95. Gc 0.64 -> 0.84; WM at ceiling across ages.
limits: No CIs or repeated runs; WM and speed only approximated by interface controls; open-weight models barely changed.
agent_relevance: Plain persona prompts do not lower working memory; limits must be enforced by the loop, not stated.

source: ChildSafe: LLM safety across child development stages, arXiv 2510.05484 (2025)
finding: Four simulated child agents (6-8, 9-11, 12-14, 15-17) labelled with Piagetian stages; 4 models scored on safety.
numbers: Composite GPT-5 0.777, Claude Sonnet 4 0.762, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.720, DeepSeek-V3.1 0.698. High-safety share 42%, 39%, 14%, 12%. Ages 6-8 lowest; 11.5% gap to 9-11.
limits: Internal count and score inconsistencies (GPT-5 6-8 score 0.805 vs 0.738; 240 vs 1,200 responses). Prompt text not shown.
agent_relevance: Piaget used only as a persona label; not evidence about reasoning.

source: Language Models Do Not Have Human-Like Working Memory, arXiv 2505.10571 (2025)
finding: 17 LLMs fail tasks that need a privately held item: number guessing, yes-no deduction, math magic. CoT or external memory fixes some.
numbers: Number guessing: most models sum of Yes-probabilities 0 (ideal 1); LLaMA-3.1-405B 1.195. Yes-No Deduction: GPT-4o 173/200 trials contradicted; GPT-4o-Mini 200/200. Math magic: GPT-4o 2.0% -> 20.7% with CoT; o3-Mini 96.7%; DeepSeek-R1 100%; QwQ-32B 90%.
limits: One prompt per task; hidden state unobservable; no human scores. 'Architectural deficiency' is interpretive.
agent_relevance: Working memory in LLMs is the context window: write held items to an explicit state. Supports a scratch state in the schema.

source: Strong Memory, Weak Control: Executive Functioning in LLMs, arXiv 2504.02789 (2025)
finding: Neo-Piagetian split: LLMs have strong memory span but weak attention control (flanker) and flexibility (WCST).
numbers: Forward span up to 50 digits ~0.99; backward span d=15 0.21 (Gemma-9B). Params vs span r=0.82. Flanker incongruent 40-60% vs humans 93-96%. WCST 0.29-0.53 vs humans ~0.77. Reasoning raised Llama-8B flanker 0.471 -> 0.910 and Qwen 0.638 -> 0.985.
limits: Human baselines from published norms; 30 prompt variants gave wide spread; table/model list mismatches.
agent_relevance: Control, not memory, is the weak part, which favours scaffolds that force inhibition and rule-switch checks.

source: Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study (n-back), arXiv 2305.03731
finding: ChatGPT shows an n-back capacity limit near n=3 on verbal task; GPT-4 stays above threshold at n=1-3.
numbers: ChatGPT verbal d' about 1 at n=3. Spatial 3x3: 1-back p~1.9e-9 above 1, 2-back p~0.94, 3-back p~0.97 not. GPT-4 d' above 1 at all n (p~9.3e-10).
limits: Exact d' only in figures; GPT-4 tested to n=3 only; no direct human stats.
agent_relevance: Capacity limit exists but is task-bound; no fixed Pascual-Leone style span.

source: Fesser et al. (2026) Evaluating Relational Reasoning in LLMs with REL (ICML), arXiv 2604.12176
finding: Halford's relational complexity (neo-Piagetian) predicts LLM failure: accuracy falls with arity even at fixed entity count.
numbers: 3 models (Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2). RPM/RPT accuracy drops 45% from RC 3 to 9. Biology homoplasy: 35% at N=4 to 1% at N=25; RC explains 24% (Claude), 32% (Gemini), 44% (GPT) of variance. A7 (RC=6) about 12% = chance.
limits: Multiple choice, synthetic tasks, no human baseline in the text read; appendix (open weights) not read.
agent_relevance: Best fit to our need: split tasks so no step binds more than about 3-4 items at once.

source: Fesser et al. (2026) REL: inference-time interventions, arXiv 2604.12176
finding: More test-time compute and one-shot examples do not remove the arity limit.
numbers: Token budgets 4,096-16,384: +2-3% on A4/A5; chemistry change ~0.4%. One-shot ICL: C1 77.0 (+6.6), C2 43.3 (+3.4), C3 32.7 (+6.0); order by RC unchanged. RDKit tool on C3: recall 0.094.
limits: ICL on 10% of tasks only; tool test only one task.
agent_relevance: Decomposition into low-arity subproblems is the lever, not longer thinking.

source: Shultz (1996) A Generative Neural Network Analysis of Conservation
finding: Cascade-correlation networks that grow hidden units simulate five conservation findings: acquisition, problem-size, discrete advantage, length bias, screening.
numbers: Five phenomena reproduced; no sample numbers in abstract.
limits: Abstract only; small toy networks, not a language model.
agent_relevance: Older AI model that gets stage-like shifts from capacity growth; relevant to adding structure when a task fails.

source: Shultz (2003/2006) constructive neural network accounts of Piagetian transitions (search snippet)
finding: Maps assimilation to forward propagation, accommodation to output-weight training, equilibration to error reduction; sibling-descendant variant matches earlier conservation results with fewer layers.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Seen only in a search snippet; not opened.
agent_relevance: Possible template for an adapt-on-error loop.

source: PISA: Piaget-inspired schema memory for LLM agents, arXiv 2510.15966 (2025)
finding: Agent memory with assimilation, schema evolution and schema creation beats memory baselines.
numbers: LOCOMO avg 63.58 vs Mem0 55.51 (+8.07), FullContext 68.47. AggQA medical 83.67 vs LangMem 51.02; finance 69.41 vs FullContext 70.59. Ablation: no init module -14.28 pts; no structure-aware retrieval -17.64 pts.
limits: No ablation of assimilation/evolution/creation themselves; judge model unspecified; own benchmark.
agent_relevance: A direct Piaget method inside an agent loop; gains come from schema structure, not the stage idea.

source: CAM: Constructivist agentic memory for LLM reading comprehension, arXiv 2510.05520 (2025)
finding: Piaget-inspired hierarchical graph memory with overlap (assimilation) and incremental updates (accommodation) gives about +3.0% over RAPTOR/GraphRAG.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini. NovelQA ACC-L 52.3 vs 47.8; QMSum 57.6 vs 53.9; MultiHop-RAG EM 72.8 vs 69.4. Without hierarchy NovelQA 46.7; without flexibility 50.3. Batch integration ~4x faster.
limits: Hyperparameters set by hand; fine-grained mode costs 3x more.
agent_relevance: Evidence that incremental schema update works in agents; modest gains.

source: Backward digit span as LLM working-memory benchmark (escholarship), seen in search
finding: Search summary says backward digit span correlates with Raven's and ARC-AGI-1.
numbers: No numbers read.
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Possible cheap capacity probe for the agent's model.
